Maya (Design): recapping today's quick design review for the model catalog compare experiment. want to try a top-aligned compact filter chip bar instead of the left rail to reduce horizontal real estate on laptops. sketch uploaded: https://figma.redwood/s/top-chip-bar
Omar (PM): ok but will new users miss filters? need an affordance that signals filters exist.
Maya (Design): idea: show a subtle badge on the catalog title when filters are available + an onboarding tooltip on first visit.
Jules (Frontend): implemented prototype; chips wrap and the table header shifts height which breaks column alignment. possible fixes: fixed header height or reserve header space with CSS vars.
Priya (A11y): chips must be keyboard-focusable buttons with aria-pressed and clear focus state. tooltips need accessible implementation (aria-describedby + role=tooltip).
Maya (Design): compact pin UX: show full "Pinned to 3.4.1" on desktop, shrink to just "3.4.1" pill on narrow widths. keep a hover tooltip with context.
Omar (PM): pins should be a single-click toggle + undo snackbar. we don't want a modal for single pins.
Jules (Frontend): backend returns version string so no extra roundtrip. i'll add undo toast and ensure undo is keyboard actionable.
Priya (A11y): snackbar must receive focus when it appears or be reachable via skip link; add a visible focusable "Undo" button.
Maya (Design): performance badges: switch from color-only to icon+label where space allows. tooltip shows latency percentile (server provides this). color choices must be colorblind-friendly.
Jules (Frontend): adding percentile field to the model payload is trivial. caution: rendering many tooltips hurts perf; we'll lazy-init tooltip content.
Omar (PM): filter state should persist for the session but scoped per org+catalog path. avoids confusion when switching contexts.
Maya (Design): final asks: 1) chip bar layout + sticky collapse, 2) compact pin copy behavior, 3) accessible badges + tooltips, 4) session-scoped filter persistence behind a flag.
preview-bot: Preview available at https://staging.redwood/catalog/compact-experiment PR:4601
Maya (Design): thanks team, i'll update figma and add accessibility notes. Jules please tag me on the PR for a quick visual pass. :thumbsup:
